findings.summary: The physiological commitment was reduced to a possibility.

evidence.baseline: This is not metaphor; it is the documented neurophysiology of the sympathetic state. Under threat, attention collapses toward the immediate, the defensive, the short-term. The visual field literally narrows.
evidence.shipped: Threat can narrow attention toward immediate danger. Poverty, precarity, violence, trauma, exhaustion, and chronic uncertainty can shorten the horizon within which choices remain possible.

findings.diagnosis: The baseline claims documented physiology and stakes the link on it; the shipped version retreats to can twice in two sentences, which is the sterile-hedging shape the catalog names when the knowledge is not in fact uncertain at that grain. Whether the tunnel-vision literature supports literally narrows is CTD-0009's verification work, and the flag belongs there rather than diffused into hedges.

findings.summary: The extractive-economy paragraph, the link's economic half, was replaced by its own rebuttal.

evidence.baseline: The farmer trapped in debt cannot afford to perceive the long-term health of his soil; he must extract this year's yield to survive this year, even though the extraction guarantees next year's failure.
evidence.shipped: A farmer in debt may understand the future of the soil perfectly and still be forced by the terms of a loan to extract from it. Inner work cannot substitute for changing those terms.

findings.diagnosis: The shipped sentences are the strongest objection the first link faces: constraint can bind while perception is intact. But the pass installed the objection in place of the claim, so the shipped section argues against a link it no longer states. The baseline is restored; the objection is preserved here and put to the author, because a counterargument this good deserves to be answered in the text rather than to replace it.

evidence.baseline: The chronic-threat fence and the presence-definition fence.

findings.diagnosis: Both fences became comma chains whose spines hold, a nervous system in a state of chronic threat is a nervous system with a narrowed aperture, and presence does the opposite.
